questions: Has your walking changed noticeably from how you usually walk?
Do you take short, shuffling steps?
Do your feet ever feel stuck to the floor when you start walking or turn?
Do you have difficulty turning around?
Have you fallen or nearly fallen recently?
Do you feel unsteady or lose your balance while walking?
Do you have slowness or stiffness in your arms or legs?
Do you have a tremor when your hands or legs are relaxed?
Is one side of your body weaker than the other?
Do you have numbness or tingling in either leg or foot?
Do you have pain in your back, hips, knees, ankles, or feet when walking?
Do you feel dizzy or light-headed when you stand up?
Did this walking problem begin suddenly?
Have you ever had a stroke, head injury, or other neurological illness?
Have you recently started or changed any medications?

results: 1. deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal reflexes, FLEXOR plantar responses, no clonus
2. tandem gait: better than free walking
3. walking backward: the scissoring DISAPPEARS on walking backward; in spasticity it persists
4. gait with a distracting or automatic task (dancing, counting backwards): the pattern changes or normalises
5. muscle tone (spasticity, rigidity, paratonia): normal tone on passive movement despite the scissoring gait
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional neurological symptom disorder presenting as a functional (psychogenic) scissoring gait

Alternatives: Bilateral lower-limb dystonia causing a scissoring gait  
Alternatives: Early upper-motor-neuron disorder, such as cervical myelopathy or multiple sclerosis  
Alternatives: Parkinsonian gait disorder
